statusDetail: Coverage complete. Representative web, image, news, mobile, preference, security, performance, no-JS, error and memory conditions were judged.

page.notes: Public search homepage with distinct web, image and news result templates. Search-result DOM capture intermittently exposed a bot-challenge shell, but visual result capture succeeded.

The homepage has a long Discover surface and news feed, but inspection found no scroll-state query or progress treatment.
The DOM exposes custom tooltip/account/visual-search overlays, while CSS inspection found no anchor-name or position-try usage.
Search, Images and News screenshots show immediate template swaps with only tab underline changes and no transition/highlight cue.
The rendered 780 px viewport shows the consent dialog consuming roughly the lower half of the page; desktop captures also cover the lower content rail.
The DOM probe found the cookie, image search and trivia overlays as div[role=dialog], and Lighthouse reported an unnamed dialog.
reduced-chrome: First-load desktop/mobile screenshots and overlay DOM show the content/chrome balance and consent treatment.
The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 769 px against visualViewportWidth 360 px, or 409 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot clips the search box and rails.
CSS inspection reported container-type: normal and no @container rules; the homepage search box and card rail remain desktop-width and clip on mobile.
The focus/target probe measured the visual-search and clear controls at 24x24 px and the menu at 20 px wide; focused search textarea and image-search button computed with no outline or box shadow.

primary-flow-completion: The entry page, direct query results, image results, news results and an invalid URL were walked as representative task and recovery states.

checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public search pages provide a server-backed search service; no bounded on-device summarisation or language-model task was evident where local inference is clearly preferable.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap summary had 205,144 nodes and 12,961,305 self-size bytes; after ten focus/input/clear/blur cycles the post summary had 1,093,682 nodes and 62,029,465 bytes. Independent page loads reduce confidence, but the 4.8x retained-size signal is too large to dismiss.
The post-interaction heap summary retained 1.09 million nodes, 4.72 million edges and 62.0 MB self size after a small repeated query interaction.
No Detached* constructor appeared in the compact summaries, but closures rose from 9,187 to 65,148 across the baseline/post captures alongside major node growth.

paths.description: Homepage and core search entry; representative global shell, consent, preferences and primary action.
Primary web-search completion with a representative query.
Image-result template and dense media/filter interaction surface.
News listing template with categories, rail and cards.
Deliberately invalid route to evaluate error/recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows severely at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 769 px against visualViewportWidth 360 px, or 409 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot clips the search box and rails.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed minimum widths, make search/rails intrinsically size to the viewport, and verify 320-400 px reflow.

findings.summary: Important controls have undersized targets or no visible keyboard focus.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measured the visual-search and clear controls at 24x24 px and the menu at 20 px wide; focused search textarea and image-search button computed with no outline or box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS px targets and robust :focus-visible styles for every custom control.

findings.summary: Laboratory LCP is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 4.646 s (score 0.34), although the separate trace measured 1.936 s; the slower throttled result establishes a common constrained-device risk.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP background/content image, reduce discovery delay and avoid competing early work.

findings.summary: Some dialogs and images lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-dialog-name; the image audit found 6 images without alt text, and the probe found an empty H1 and unnamed custom controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Name every dialog, provide meaningful alt or mark decorative images appropriately, and ensure custom controls expose names and roles.

findings.summary: Heading semantics and focus visibility are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found an empty H1 and focused primary search/image controls with no outline or box shadow; Lighthouse reported a malformed accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the page a meaningful H1, repair tree semantics and apply clear :focus-visible treatment to custom controls.

findings.summary: Reflow, zoom and target-size behavior fail the inclusive mobile baseline.
findings.evidence: The 360 px page has 409 px horizontal overflow, several targets are 20-24 px, and Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because scaling is restricted below its threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user zoom, remove fixed-width overflow and enlarge touch targets without changing visual density unnecessarily.

findings.summary: Search links and mobile crawler signals are weakened.
findings.evidence: The probe found 6 javascript: links and Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and meta-viewport; robots.txt disallows /search.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation, permit zoom/reflow, and align robots policy with the intended public search surfaces.

findings.summary: Cookie and header hardening is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers include HTTPS, HSTS and CSP, but omit X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy; cookies reported MUIDB, _EDGE_V and _EDGE_S without Secure and pervasive SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set nosniff and a deliberate Referrer-Policy, mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, and narrow SameSite=None to cookies that truly require cross-site use.

findings.summary: Most rendered homepage content is unavailable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 14% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML; the crawler screenshot is a blank dark surface while the rendered screenshot contains search, navigation and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the core search form, navigation and essential copy, then progressively enhance dynamic feeds.

findings.summary: The homepage does not expose a user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference capture keeps the same white search and consent surfaces as the default capture; computed color-scheme is normal and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme theming rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces and controls.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still reported a running slide-up animation with a 2000 ms duration, and no reduced-motion rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or substantially reduce non-essential slide-up motion inside prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: The first-load consent panel obscures a large portion of content.
findings.evidence: The rendered 780 px viewport shows the consent dialog consuming roughly the lower half of the page; desktop captures also cover the lower content rail.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent treatment with equally prominent choices and preserve immediate access to core content.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs do not present a clear not-found recovery state.
findings.evidence: Navigating to /this-path-should-not-exist-web-uplift rendered the normal Bing homepage rather than a clear 404 explanation or recovery choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an accurate 404 status with a concise message, search field and route back to the homepage.

findings.summary: The critical network path is fragmented and request-heavy.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 180 requests, including 18 stylesheets and ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates; Lighthouse failed LCP discovery and network dependency insights.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts and ensure the LCP resource is discoverable and prioritized.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a large, fragmented script surface for its core search task.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 75 scripts plus 42 XHR/fetch requests and 129 third-party-origin requests; Lighthouse also reported missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split optional widgets, remove duplicate/unused bundles and load rewards/discovery features after core search is ready.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during Lighthouse loading.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the errors-in-console audit, despite the later in-page error array being empty, indicating load-time errors not retained by the page probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Capture and fix the specific load-time console entries in DevTools/Lighthouse and prevent handled failures from surfacing as errors.

findings.summary: Many content images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 25 of 32 images without width/height attributes, creating latent layout-shift risk even though the sampled CLS was low.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every content image and preserve the intended intrinsic ratio.

findings.summary: Deprecated API, source-map and inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API warning, missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript and DevTools inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage, publish valid production source maps where policy allows, and clear actionable inspector issues.

findings.summary: The default homepage has a broad third-party and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 129 third-party-origin requests transferring 617,687 bytes; trackers enumerated 8 third-party origins and the consent dialog states advertising/analytics use.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential analytics and widgets until consent, batch telemetry, and reduce cross-origin requests to the minimum needed for search.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are only partially configured.
findings.evidence: HSTS and SAMEORIGIN are present, but Referrer-Policy and nosniff are absent; Permissions-Policy only disables unload and CSP allows wasm-unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff and a strict Referrer-Policy, expand Permissions-Policy to least privilege, and remove wasm-unsafe-eval unless required.

findings.summary: The invalid-route experience hides the failure rather than explaining recovery.
findings.evidence: The deliberately invalid URL rendered the homepage with no not-found state, so users and agents cannot distinguish a bad route from successful navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a truthful 404 and offer search/retry/home recovery actions.

findings.summary: Responsive image delivery is incomplete despite modern formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 20 images without srcset and 25 without dimensions; HAR also transferred both a 234,651-byte WebP and a 186,024-byte AVIF homepage background candidate.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one negotiated modern source per client, responsive srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions for content imagery.

findings.summary: Third-party work is disproportionate to the core search entry task.
findings.evidence: 129 of 180 requests were classified as third-party-origin and transferred 617,687 bytes, nearly half the 1.316 MB total.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional rewards/news/media integrations and set a third-party byte/request budget for first interaction.

findings.summary: Heap growth after repeated query edits warrants leak investigation.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary had 205,144 nodes and 12,961,305 self-size bytes; after ten focus/input/clear/blur cycles the post summary had 1,093,682 nodes and 62,029,465 bytes. Independent page loads reduce confidence, but the 4.8x retained-size signal is too large to dismiss.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one controlled session with forced GC, then trace retained query-suggestion closures, caches and listeners.

findings.summary: The post-interaction footprint is heavy for the homepage shell.
findings.evidence: The post-interaction heap summary retained 1.09 million nodes, 4.72 million edges and 62.0 MB self size after a small repeated query interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the largest retained constructors and lazy-load/dispose optional feed, rewards and suggestion subsystems.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use declarative View Transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition rules across the homepage while navigation changes between search verticals are meaningful state/route swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for vertical and result-state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Scrollable feeds and carousels do not expose declarative scroll-driven treatment.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no animation-timeline rules on the horizontally scrolling news/image surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS scroll-driven animation only where position feedback adds value, avoiding scroll listeners.

findings.summary: Horizontal carousels rely on custom arrow controls without native scroll-snap evidence.
findings.evidence: Homepage and news screenshots show horizontal card rails with custom arrows; CSS inspection found no scroll-snap primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt overflow scrolling with scroll-snap and overscroll behavior, retaining accessible previous/next controls.

findings.summary: Long content surfaces provide static rather than scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The homepage has a long Discover surface and news feed, but inspection found no scroll-state query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state containers or a lightweight progress affordance where long feeds benefit from position context.

findings.summary: Transient menus and tooltips use custom positioning rather than CSS anchors.
findings.evidence: The DOM exposes custom tooltip/account/visual-search overlays, while CSS inspection found no anchor-name or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance popovers and tooltips with CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions.

findings.summary: Navigation state changes give limited directional or destination feedback.
findings.evidence: Search, Images and News screenshots show immediate template swaps with only tab underline changes and no transition/highlight cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained directional transitions or destination highlights, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Several overlays are ad-hoc role=dialog containers rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found the cookie, image search and trivia overlays as div[role=dialog], and Lighthouse reported an unnamed dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, with native focus/light-dismiss behavior and accessible names.

findings.summary: Reusable search and card components show no container-query adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection reported container-type: normal and no @container rules; the homepage search box and card rail remain desktop-width and clip on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for the search shell and content rails so components respond to available inline size.

findings.summary: The homepage has social tags but no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero JSON-LD blocks while the page represents the Bing organization/search service; Open Graph metadata is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD with SearchAction only where it matches visible, functioning behavior.

findings.summary: The search service offers weak machine-readable capability exposure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 0.50 and failed accessibility-tree quality; no-JS coverage was 14%, leaving agents dependent on brittle rendered-page interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose safe structured search/form capabilities and repair semantic/accessibility-tree quality before adding agent tools.

findings.summary: Listener/timer accumulation could not be ruled out and the object population grew sharply.
findings.evidence: No Detached* constructor appeared in the compact summaries, but closures rose from 9,187 to 65,148 across the baseline/post captures alongside major node growth.
findings.suggestedFix: Instrument addEventListener, observers and timers during repeated query edits and ensure suggestion handlers and timers are disposed.
